candidate.name: local-stack
candidate.delivery: run-owned Docker Compose system plane; native Codex sandbox for evaluated projects
candidate.selection_limit: The existing Compose definition is authorized as the local OpenBox system, but it requires a run-owned project name, fresh resources, loopback-only published ports, exact identity checks, and project-scoped teardown before it can satisfy the governed-run gate.

commands.command: git -C <local-stack|backend|core> rev-parse HEAD; branch --show-current; describe --always --dirty; status --short
commands.result: Exact commits recorded; all three candidate worktrees were clean.

commands.command: find/grep/sed over the bounded policy, governance API, OPA, persistence, compose, bootstrap, preflight, and teardown sources listed in inputs
commands.result: Static identity, storage, policy publication, event-history, credential, and teardown paths were qualified without executing them.
The review is bound to the exact source bytes above.

commands.command: docker compose -p openbox-assurance-se0701 -f compose.local.yml -f compose.governed.override.yml config --format json
commands.result: The rendered project has one run-owned network, four run-owned volumes, and only backend, Core, OPA, and Keycloak published on literal 127.0.0.1 ports.

commands.command: docker compose ... up -d; bounded health, database, Redis, Temporal, identity, policy, and OPA probes
commands.result: Fresh exact-source services became healthy; one test organization control key registered one signed KMS agent; signed Core identity verification passed; one harmless ALLOW policy propagated to OPA; no evaluated project or model was launched.

commands.command: docker compose ... down -v --remove-orphans; exact resource, listener, and pre-existing-stack identity rechecks
commands.result: All run-owned containers, network, volumes, and loopback listeners were removed. Pre-existing openbox-local container and volume identity digests were byte-identical before and after.

threat_review.real_decision_path: Core POST /api/v1/governance/evaluate authenticates an agent token, runs the GovernanceEventWorkflow, evaluates the agent's active policy through OPA, persists the governance event and policy evaluation, and starts observability plus non-ALLOW notification/realtime paths.
threat_review.policy_authority: Backend POST /agent/:agentId/policies is an authenticated control-plane mutation. Creation deactivates prior agent policies, persists a new current version, rebuilds the organization bundle, uploads it to shared MinIO, and OPA polls that shared bundle.
threat_review.storage: The provided environment shares persistent Postgres, Redis, MinIO, Keycloak, and Temporal services. Policy, governance-event, evaluation, session, trust, observability, and attestation state is not scoped to a disposable run store.
threat_review.credentials: The harness control token is organization-scoped and can create/read agents and policies and manage sessions. The project agent receives a persistent API key and signing key; a test-looking prefix is not an isolation proof.
threat_review.endpoint_sentinel: The existing testbed accepts ambient overrides for backend, Core, OPA, database container, database name, and organization. It supplies local defaults but does not fail closed on non-loopback coordinates or fingerprint the service instances before mutation.
threat_review.event_history: Core stores governance_events and policy_evaluations and can create sessions, Merkle leaves, attestations, trust triggers, observability records, realtime events, and notifications. These are product histories, not an ephemeral decision-only transcript.
threat_review.teardown: testbed/99-teardown.sh explicitly keeps every database row and testbed audit/session state, deactivates the credential and database policy flags, and states that OPA keeps serving the last compiled bundle. local-stack/scripts/down.sh preserves all data by default; --volumes deletes the entire shared stack, not one run.
threat_review.execution_boundary: Docker Compose is authorized only for the run-owned local OpenBox system plane. The evaluated Mastra project remains outside Compose and may run only in the exact qualified native Codex sandbox; this qualification did not launch a project or model.

production_contamination_sentinels.fresh_state: The run began with zero agents, API keys, policies, governance events, policy evaluations, sessions, attestations, spans, and project registrations in its fresh Postgres volume. Temporal returned an empty workflow list.

test_identity.credential_files: Control token, agent environment, and developer identity files were task-owned mode 0600. Credential values and their digests are not retained in this evidence.

production_contamination_sentinels.history: After the bounded identity/policy proof, governance events, policy evaluations, sessions, attestations, spans, project registrations, and Temporal workflows remained zero. Redis held only bounded queue metadata, the run agent nonce, and its local-KMS public-key entry; no values were retained.
production_contamination_sentinels.cleanup: Project-scoped down -v --remove-orphans removed every run-owned container, network, and volume. Ports 48080, 48081, 48086, and 48181 had no listener afterward. Task-owned credential files were moved recoverably to Trash after their backing identity and policy stores were deleted. Source-built images were retained for the next phase because they contain no run state or credentials.

recommendation: Reuse the existing local-stack Compose definition under a unique run-owned project name with fresh volumes, loopback-only ports, test-only identities, exact pre/post contamination sentinels, and project-scoped down --volumes cleanup. Keep the Mastra application inside the qualified native Codex sandbox; Docker is not an execution sandbox for the evaluated project.

independent_review.result: threat_model_accepted; live isolation verified by root
independent_review.finding: The stock shared project is insufficient, but the exact override closes the lifecycle boundary with a unique Compose project, fresh volumes, loopback-only publications, exact-source images, test-only identity, and project-scoped erasure. The project sandbox remains native and separate.

limits: This proves system-plane isolation and cleanup for one macOS Docker Desktop/Compose tuple; it does not prove a governed BLOCK or a project run.
The harmless ALLOW policy was an isolation/lifecycle sentinel only. No candidate proposal was loaded and no BLOCK was synthesized or claimed.
The first cached-image attempt exposed source/image drift and was destroyed without registering an agent or policy; only the exact source-built images are accepted for subsequent Phase 07 work.
The pre-existing openbox-local resources were proven unchanged by identity metadata, not by reading their contents.
Docker Compose is allowed for the OpenBox system plane only. It is not an evaluated-project sandbox and must not be presented as one.
